entries.name: Farmstead
entries.desc: Terraced fields and a tithe barn. Grain, best on open plain.
entries.trade_off: Feeds armies, but a devastated province loses the harvest entirely.

entries.name: Sawmill
entries.desc: A water-driven saw. Timber, best in forest.
entries.trade_off: Clears trees, which makes the province easier to cross for armies.

entries.name: Mine
entries.desc: Shafts and a smelter. Ore from mountain and hill.
entries.trade_off: Hard labour: +1 unrest per turn in this province.

entries.name: Saltworks
entries.desc: Evaporation pans. Salt feeds trade, keeps rations edible and slows attrition.
entries.trade_off: Only worthwhile on marsh or a salt pan.

entries.name: Scriptorium
entries.desc: Scribes copy, annotate and argue. Ink drives research.
entries.trade_off: Pamphlets stir the town: +2 unrest per turn.

entries.name: Market
entries.desc: Stalls, scales and a customs shed. Coin, and an end point for trade routes.
entries.trade_off: Trade routes can be raided, and a market is a juicy target.

entries.name: Barracks
entries.desc: Trains foot, archers, banners and healers; one recruit per level per turn.
entries.trade_off: Soldiers keep order (-2 unrest) but eat into the treasury.

entries.name: Stable
entries.trade_off: Horses eat grain; best kept to open country.

entries.name: Siege Workshop
entries.desc: Builds rams, throwers and other engines.
entries.trade_off: Engines are slow and useless in the open; they win sieges.

entries.name: Granary
entries.desc: A supply depot: armies within three steps draw rations. Raises the stockpile limit.
entries.trade_off: A depot attracts raiders; if it falls, the supply line dies with it.

entries.name: Watchtower
entries.desc: Sees two provinces out. Fog of war is a real enemy.

entries.name: Fortress Works
entries.desc: Walls and a stronger garrison per level. Rams and throwers are needed to breach it.
entries.trade_off: Expensive to keep; a fort cannot move, but it ends rushes.

entries.name: Hall of Hours
entries.desc: A shared clock tower where houses meet to settle their dates. Calms the province and its neighbours.
